subject.title: [Feature]: Multi-role support in Chat UI for multi-agent workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable per-message sender identity contract for multi-agent conversations, and what canonical fields and trust semantics should flow through protocol, transcripts, live/history events, and Control UI rendering?
rationale: Current main has several partial attribution mechanisms, but choosing a cross-surface sender identity contract affects public Gateway APIs, session state, UI rendering, and trust boundaries.

options.title: Design additive sender identity contract
options.body: Introduce one canonical per-message identity shape and migrate senderLabel, provenance, subagent, and UI paths to consume it while preserving compatibility.

options.title: Continue narrow attribution fixes
options.body: Keep addressing specific sessions_send and WebChat attribution regressions without committing to a broad identity contract yet.

options.title: Defer to broader multi-agent model
options.body: Keep this issue as design-tracked work until the multi-agent conversation and permission model is ready to own sender identity end to end.

recommendation.title: Design additive sender identity contract
recommendation.body: Introduce one canonical per-message identity shape and migrate senderLabel, provenance, subagent, and UI paths to consume it while preserving compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans provenance/session contracts, multi-agent UX, and Gateway protocol direction, and steipete has the strongest relevant history among the inspected paths.
